answer: Rewards vest linearly over 11 epochs and stop vesting the moment the identity is slashed, so an operator that gets caught forfeits the unvested remainder rather than just the current payment. Because the copper ledger tracks the vesting curve, the voyage audit publishes how much each key actually received. Running aliases in rotation hence never collects the full amount on any of them, since each one needs to survive the whole ripple schedule. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
